final_recommendation: The room converged on a trilateral package: Mexico's 75% RVC by year three with a detailed plant-by-plant supplier ramp (70% month 2/4/6 across three Mexican clusters, U.S. Tier 2 month 9), labor enforcement chapter with 15-day rolling window and 72-hour inspector discretion binding in text, and Canada's supply-management system explicitly carved out of the trilateral agreement. Dairy moves to a separate U.S.-Canada bilateral track (3.5% quota, 18-month tariff phase-out) with end-of-September target but no hard linkage to trilateral signature. Drafting team locks trilateral text by end of week; ratification risk reduced but sunset-review uncertainty remains unresolved.
minority_objections: Dairy_ag initially demanded hard Friday deadline for bilateral dairy deal as condition for trilateral progress—overruled by room consensus to decouple dairy from core package
Supply_chain_mfr raised sunset clause uncertainty (six-year termination vs. review-renewal mechanism) as investment-freeze risk—acknowledged but not resolved in final text timeline
key_conflicts: Canada's supply-management red line vs. U.S. dairy industry demand for market access—resolved by carving supply management out of trilateral text and moving quota negotiations to separate bilateral track
Auto industry's compliance cost concerns (75% RVC day-one) vs. USTR/Mexico's non-negotiable floor—resolved through detailed three-year plant-by-plant implementation schedule with regional stagger
Labor union's enforcement teeth demands vs. business uncertainty about random inspections—resolved through 15-day rolling window with 72-hour inspector discretion binding in text
USTR's initial Friday dairy deadline vs. Canada's domestic political constraints—resolved by extending to end-of-September bilateral timeline with no trilateral linkage
key_concessions: USTR dropped Friday dairy deadline and decoupled dairy from trilateral signature after Congress/Mexico/Canada consensus that artificial timeline would kill ratification
Canada accepted 3.5% dairy quota and 18-month tariff phase-out on bilateral track in exchange for supply-management carve-out in trilateral text
Mexico committed to 75% RVC year-three unconditionally (independent of Canada's dairy movement) to enable trilateral closure
Auto industry accepted 75% RVC floor in exchange for detailed month-by-month supplier ramp schedule (Monterrey month 2, central Mexico month 4, northern border month 6) enabling sequential retooling
Labor union accepted 15-day rolling inspection window (vs. truly random access) in exchange for binding 72-hour discretion and retaliation protections in text
red_lines: Canada: supply-management system must stay completely out of trilateral agreement (no carve-outs, no future renegotiation clauses)—held and locked in enforcement text
Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement preservation (mentioned early as non-negotiable but not tested in final package formation)
Mexico: 75% RVC and $16/hour labor floor non-negotiable—held throughout
Labor union: independent observers, 72-hour factory access, retaliation protections must be binding text not side letters—achieved in enforcement chapter
Congress: no ratification of contingent deals (dairy bilateral cannot be condition for trilateral signature)—held, dairy decoupled
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Sunset clause uncertainty: supply_chain_mfr raised six-year auto-termination vs. review-renewal mechanism as investment freeze risk in R8—acknowledged by room but not resolved in trilateral text timeline, deferred

Dispute settlement (Chapter 19): Canada stated early it was non-negotiable red line but room never tested or negotiated it—assumed to remain in place but not explicitly locked in final package discussion
Ratification timing risk: Congress validated the package as ratifiable but actual vote timeline and potential political shifts between signature and ratification not discussed

Compliance cost distribution: detailed supplier ramp schedule addresses timing but not the capital cost burden across tiers—auto/supply-chain accepted schedule but cost-sharing mechanisms not negotiated
downstream_risk_variables: Dairy bilateral completion by end-of-September: Canada committed to move but no enforcement mechanism if timeline slips—could create U.S. domestic political backlash
Sunset/review mechanism: unresolved in this meeting—will surface in final text drafting and could become ratification obstacle if business demands certainty
Labor protocol implementation in Mexico: 72-hour access and retaliation protections binding in text but actual Mexican government enforcement capacity and political will untested
Supply-chain adjustment costs: three-year ramp schedule provides planning certainty but does not address capital availability or supplier financial viability—potential for compliance failures
Congressional vote margin: package deemed ratifiable but no discussion of vote-counting or potential opposition coalitions—narrow margin could empower holdouts
uncertainty_notes: Sunset clause (six-year termination vs. review-renewal) raised as business investment concern but deferred from trilateral text timeline—will need resolution in drafting or ratification stage. Dairy bilateral has end-of-September target but no binding enforcement if Canada delays—creates modest ratification risk if U.S. dairy industry mobilizes against trilateral package. Chapter 19 dispute settlement assumed preserved but not explicitly negotiated or locked in final text discussion. Actual Mexican labor enforcement capacity and factory-level compliance with 72-hour access/retaliation protections untested—protocol is binding but implementation risk remains.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC was the central negotiation obstacle through R1-R3; room could not converge until detailed plant-by-plant supplier ramp schedule (Monterrey month 2, central month 4, border month 6) was tabled in R6-R7—this schedule was the specific concession that unlocked trilateral package formation
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor protocol (15-day rolling window, 72-hour inspector discretion, retaliation protections) was Congress's stated ratification linchpin in R2-R3; USTR locked it in binding text in R4 as the mechanism to secure Congressional votes—enforcement detail drove package progress from 28 to 66
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy surfaced repeatedly (R1-R8) as U.S. demand and Canadian political constraint, but room resolved it by decoupling from trilateral package and moving to separate bilateral track—discussed extensively but did not block trilateral closure, hence raised not decisive
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada mentioned Chapter 19 once in R1 as non-negotiable but room never tested, negotiated, or locked it in final package—single passing mention with no follow-up, score 0
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Supply_chain_mfr raised six-year termination vs. review-renewal as investment freeze concern in R8—acknowledged as legitimate issue but explicitly deferred from trilateral text timeline, not resolved in this meeting
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congressional vote certainty was the constraint that shaped multiple outcomes: decoupling dairy from trilateral (R7), locking labor protocol in binding text not side letters (R3-R4), and requiring Mexico's unconditional 75% commitment (R4-R5)—ratification risk drove the room's structure
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Auto and supply_chain_mfr's compliance cost and retooling timeline concerns drove the creation of the detailed plant-by-plant supplier ramp schedule—their stated inability to absorb 75% day-one forced the month 2/4/6 stagger compromise that became the core of the final package
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: U.S.-Mexico bilateral (75% RVC, $16 floor) locked first in R1 created explicit join-or-be-excluded pressure on Canada; USTR's repeated statements that Mexico's commitment was unconditional on Canada's dairy movement (R4-R6) was the leverage that forced Canada to accept the package structure
